requirement.text: As a user, I want to select any color on the screen, so that I can get its RGB values.

classification.rationale: Selecting any color on the screen to get RGB values describes a general UI utility typical of desktop applications, lacking specific signals indicating a web, mobile, or AI system.

rounds.text_checked: As a user, I want to select any color on the screen, so that I can get its RGB values.

test_strategy.rationale: Equivalence partitioning applies because screen locations and RGB color values can be partitioned into valid pixel regions vs. out-of-bounds selections and distinct color types. Boundary value analysis applies to test extreme RGB channel bounds (0 and 255 for R, G, and B) and screen edge coordinates. Use case testing applies because the requirement describes an end-to-end user interaction flow of selecting a screen point to retrieve its corresponding RGB color values.

test_cases.title: End-to-End Screen Color Selection and RGB Extraction
test_cases.preconditions: Color picker application is launched and ready for input.
steps: Activate the screen color selection tool.
Hover cursor over a target pixel on the screen.
Click to select the target pixel color.
Verify the displayed color information panel.
test_cases.expected_result: The application captures the precise selected screen pixel and displays its corresponding RGB values clearly to the user.

test_cases.title: Minimum Boundary RGB Channel Values (Pure Black)
test_cases.preconditions: Color picker application is active, and pure black (RGB 0,0,0) is displayed on screen.
steps: Select the pure black pixel using the color selection tool.
test_cases.expected_result: The system accurately reports RGB values of (0, 0, 0).

test_cases.title: Maximum Boundary RGB Channel Values (Pure White)
test_cases.preconditions: Color picker application is active, and pure white (RGB 255,255,255) is displayed on screen.
steps: Select the pure white pixel using the color selection tool.
test_cases.expected_result: The system accurately reports RGB values of (255, 255, 255).

test_cases.title: Screen Edge Coordinates Boundary Test
test_cases.preconditions: Color picker application is active across screen display bounds.
steps: Select a pixel at top-left screen boundary coordinate (0, 0).
Select a pixel at bottom-right screen boundary coordinate (max_x, max_y).
test_cases.expected_result: Screen edge coordinates are properly handled without throwing out-of-bounds exceptions, returning valid RGB values for both edge points.

test_cases.title: Valid Standard Color Partition Selection
test_cases.preconditions: Color picker application is active with distinct primary colors rendered.
steps: Select a pixel in a region rendered with pure Red (RGB 255, 0, 0).
Select a pixel in a region rendered with pure Green (RGB 0, 255, 0).
Select a pixel in a region rendered with pure Blue (RGB 0, 0, 255).
test_cases.expected_result: The application returns (255, 0, 0), (0, 255, 0), and (0, 0, 255) respectively for each standard color partition.

test_cases.title: Selection Cancellation Equivalence Partition
steps: Press the Escape key to cancel selection mode without picking a screen pixel.
test_cases.expected_result: Color selection mode exits cleanly without updating RGB values or causing an error state.

final_text: As a user, I want to select any color on the screen, so that I can get its RGB values.
